title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-sam-ramirez
content:
Quick notes / breadcrumbs from debugging a GPU OOM + driver/library mismatch that repro'd on a Dedicated node (p4d-ish).

Summary:
- Model: transformer-xxl-ish (approx 80B parameters in fp32, using 8-bit quant path in runtime).
- Symptom: intermittent CUDA driver/library mismatch errors followed by GPU OOM or process killed. Happens more often under high-concurrency load (batching + long context).
- Reproduced on: dedicated-GPU-1 (node-id: ded-314) and once in staging.

Steps to reproduce (local repro attempt):
1) Checkout runtime branch: feature/optimize-batching (PR #812).
2) Launch minimal worker: docker run --gpus all --shm-size=1g -it redwood/runtime:dev /bin/bash
3) Inside: python repro/gpu_oom_repro.py --model transformer-xxl --batch 12 --context 4096

Commands run and outputs:
- nvidia-smi
  Wed Nov  6 14:23:01 2024
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.10    Driver Version: 535.86.10    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
  | GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
  |  0  A100-SXM4-40GB         On   00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                    0 |

- nvcc --version
  nvcc: NVIDIA (R) Cuda compiler driver
  Copyright (c) 2005-2023 NVIDIA Corporation
  Built on Thu_Jul_13_19:14:50_PDT_2023
  Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105

- python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda)"
  2.2.0+cu121
  12.1

- pip list | grep -E 'torch|cuda|cudnn'
  torch 2.2.0+cu121
  torchvision 0.15.2+cu121
  torchaudio 2.2.0

What I saw when repro'ing:
- First run: immediate runtime error in C++ loader: CUDA driver/library mismatch: expected cuBLAS >= 13 but found 12.x (message paraphrased).
- After a few restarts, started seeing torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to dump small trace:

  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "repro/gpu_oom_repro.py", line 128, in <module>
      out = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=512, do_sample=False)
    File "/opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1501, in _call_impl
      return forward_call(*input, **kwargs)
    File "/workspace/models/transformer.py", line 342, in forward
      outputs = self.transformer_block(x, kv_cache=kv)
  torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 33.45 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 37.80 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

- dmesg showed: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus" after the driver mismatch earlier (suggests driver crash).

Commands tried to mitigate (notes on effectiveness):
- torch.cuda.empty_cache() (inside repro) -> no meaningful change, only short-lived release of cached memory.
- reduce batch size from 12 -> 6 -> 3 -> 1 -> stops OOM but throughput drops; helps confirm memory pressure cause.
- set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 -> makes failure deterministic but changes timing (slower).
- export PYTORCH_JIT=0 (was suggested in thread) -> no change.
- switched to mixed precision (amp/autocast) -> reduced mem footprint ~40% and reduced OOM frequency, but still driver crash after long run.
- pinned to driver 535.54 (downgrade) -> temporarily removed driver-mismatch messages but still saw occasional OOM under high concurrency.
- docker run with --shm-size=8g and increased ulimit memlock -> no change for device RAM but helpful for host shared memory errors.
- restarted GPU (sudo nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0) -> transiently fixed "fallen off the bus" errors until heavy load resumed.

Hypotheses / observations:
- There might be two distinct issues colliding: 1) CUDA/cuBLAS/cuDNN driver-version mismatch between container libs and host driver, 2) actual memory pressure from our batching + KV cache strategy. Driver mismatch can crash the driver, which then makes OOMs harder to reason about.
- The "reserved by PyTorch" number is high: 37.80 GiB reserved on 40 GiB GPU. That suggests default caching allocator plus a large pre-allocation from our code (maybe model_init with big buffers or aggressive kv cache). Need to grep for .to(device) calls during init.
- NCCL errors were not present in single-GPU repro, but cluster logs show NCCL timeouts in some failed runs (maybe unrelated).

Immediate next steps (actionable):
- Reconcile driver/library: Ensure container CUDA toolkit libs match host driver. Prefer images built with CUDA 12.1 if driver 535.86.10 advertises CUDA 12.1. Add test startup check: compare `nvidia-smi` CUDA Version vs `torch.version.cuda` and run a small cuBLAS test.
- Add runtime guard that rejects startup when obvious mismatch (cuBLAS version check) to avoid driver crash.
- Add memory accounting prints to runtime startup: peak reserved, allocated, free, largest_allocated_block (use torch.cuda.memory_reserved/allocated/empty_cache) before accepting traffic.
- Add forced periodic torch.cuda.empty_cache() in worker after serving large batches (temporary mitigation).
- Instrument KV cache size by max_seq and rotary embeddings to compute expected kv memory; refuse large batch+long-context combos if expected > 0.85 * device_mem.
- Reproduce with smaller model and scaled config to iterate faster.

Notes from conversation with infra/SRE (Raja):
- Raja: "We saw similar 'fallen off the bus' when GPU driver was upgraded but container base image still had older libcudnn/cublas libs. Host driver must be compatible with container libs; recommend using NVIDIA container toolkit recommended images."
- Asha: "We should add an autoscale fallback that moves requests to lower-memory model variant (8B/13B) when a node approaches 90% reserved."

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add startup cuBLAS/cuDNN compatibility check into worker (owner: Sam, due 2024-11-11).
- [ ] Add mem-accounting instrumentation and metrics (owner: Asha, due 2024-11-14).
- [ ] Create small repro with synthetic KV growth to stress memory faster (owner: Sam).
- [ ] Follow up with infra to standardize container base images for dedicated pools (Raja).

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Is our model init doing any hidden full-precision allocations temporarily? (need code audit of model load path).
- Why does driver crash only under load sometimes? Is there a specific cublas/cuDNN call ordering that triggers bug in driver 535.x? Could be a vendor bug.
- Should we implement a watchdog that restarts worker before driver becomes unstable? Risky but pragmatic.

References / pointers saved here:
- nvidia forum threads about "Xid 31 GPU fallen off the bus"
- internal confluence: confluence:gpu-debugging-runbook
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/812 (related batching changes)
- Jira: JIRA-4567 (incident ticket)

Scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Pre-warm memory in a controlled way to avoid sudden allocations during serving (gradual ramp).
- Implement per-request mem-estimator that rejects if expected allocation + current_reserved > threshold.
- Consider enabling `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False` during high-concurrency to avoid cudnn algorithm hunt spikes (though that can hurt perf).

Short session log (timestamps):
- 2024-11-06 14:10 start repro -> driver mismatch error on first run
- 2024-11-06 14:16 pinned driver -> next run started but OOM at batch 10
- 2024-11-06 14:44 CPU/gpu reset -> temporary stability
- 2024-11-07 09:30 added mixed-precision -> reduced OOM frequency but still saw dmesg Xid 31 at 09:52

If anyone else is digging in, start with: 1) nvidia-smi (host) + nvcc --version in container, 2) run small cuBLAS sample (link in runbook), 3) capture full dmesg after crash and attach to JIRA ticket.

End of notes.
